## Overview

Standalone Wero is an authenticated bank transfer in EUR. Customers connect a bank account to their Wero wallet. The May 5, 2026 method overview listed Germany for customers. On November 7 the overview lists Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. Both list the same 30 European Stripe account locations, a separate business eligibility list. Those locations are AT, BE, BG, CY, CZ, DE, DK, EE, ES, FI, FR, GR, HR, HU, IE, IS, IT, LI, LT, LU, LV, MT, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SE, SI and SK. Minimum payment amount is EUR 0.50. The maximum varies by bank and is usually determined by the customer's bank limits. See May lines 8–46, 52–85 and 123–125 and November lines 9–47, 53–86 and 122–124.

The November cross-method overview labels standalone Wero as public preview, alongside the separate iDEAL | Wero entry. The iDEAL | Wero guide sets out its own rebranding and phased switch instructions covering 2026–2027. The Netherlands buyer overlap is distinct from those migration instructions and the separate API payment method identities. The November bank-redirect matrix's unsupported manual-capture cell applies to `ideal`. See [[stripe-ideal]] and [[source-stripe-payment-methods-overview]].

## Customer authorization and payment status

When the customer selects Wero, Stripe redirects them to Wero's authentication page. They scan the QR code, open the Wero app and approve. The method overviews describe payment processing in typically under ten seconds and a redirect back. Standard payout timing is separate. In the scoped May acceptance guide, a failed payment or an authorization session without action for one hour returns the PaymentIntent to `requires_payment_method`. Verify payment status independently of the redirect and use the successful payment event for fulfillment. The November acceptance capture is a variant index. See May overview lines 115–117, November lines 114–116, and May acceptance lines 599–611 and 880–885.

## Product support and onboarding

Both overview captures list Connect, Checkout in payment mode, Payment Links and Elements. Checkout subscription or setup modes and Express Checkout Element are excluded. Neither overview lists recurring payments or disputes as supported. May lists manual capture No. November lists manual capture Yes and supplies no capture workflow, release behavior or authorization window for manual capture. See May lines 28–50 and 87–94 and November lines 29–51 and 88–95.

Both guides describe Dashboard enablement and a separate manual integration route. May invites merchants to submit an interest form to get in touch. November omits that invitation. Preview status and account eligibility still apply. November lists categories prohibited or restricted in addition to Stripe's general rules, including payment facilitators processing for sub-merchants, peer-to-peer transfers, and other named categories. The guide does not classify each bullet as prohibited versus restricted. The category condition qualifies the general Connect support label. See May lines 94–113 and November lines 95–112 and 126–143.

## Refunds

The May guide states a window of up to two years after the original payment. November specifies up to 730 days after the original payment. Both document full and partial refunds, including multiple partial refunds up to the original charge amount. See May lines 119–121 and November lines 118–120.

payments-wero.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wero describes standalone Wero as EUR authenticated bank transfer for buyers in Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands, distinct from 30 listed business-account countries (new raw lines 9-47 and 53-95). A customer connects a bank account to Wero and selects it at checkout. Stripe redirects to Wero's authentication page, the customer scans the QR and approves in the Wero app, and the payment typically processes in under ten seconds before return (new raw lines 114-124). Return is not independently verified success or payout. The overview says standard payout timing and manual capture support but gives no capture state sequence. A dated acceptance guide separately describes Intent status verification and a one-hour authentication expiry. Compared with May 5 (old raw lines 12-46 and 94-125), November expands buyer geography and changes manual capture to Yes, adds business restrictions and states 730 days for refunds. source-stripe-wero.md now dates Germany-only customers and the old capture label, and scopes the May interest-form invitation alongside Dashboard enablement.
payments-wero.Q2: The substantive changes at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wero include the five-country buyer list, standalone Wero manual capture from No to Yes, the explicit 730-day refund cutoff and added category restrictions. The interest-form invitation is removed while Dashboard activation instructions remain (old raw lines 12-46, 94-113 and 119-125; new raw lines 13-47, 95-112 and 118-143). Heading formatting and Elements quickstart destination are presentational or navigational. Preserve May Germany-only buyers separately from 30 business locations, the literal two-year refund wording, no recurring/disputes and the typical rather than guaranteed ten-second timing. The November payments overview still labels Wero public preview, while iDEAL | Wero is a separate identity with its own migration instruction and an unsupported manual-capture cell. The overlapping Netherlands buyer geography does not erase that distinction. Keep separate acceptance navigation and retain root index line 7, Stripe index lines 289 and 757 and Wero concept lines 52-53, adding a source backlink in source-stripe-wero.md and retaining both factual captures.

concept_suggestions.anchor:
Wero is a pan-European authenticated bank transfer payment method. Customers connect their bank accounts to a Wero wallet and approve payments via the Wero App. API enum: `wero`. Currently available to German customers only.

**Note**: Wero is distinct from [[stripe-ideal]] (iDEAL|Wero) — iDEAL|Wero is the Netherlands' iDEAL method rebranding to Wero infrastructure; this page covers Wero as a standalone German payment method.

**Currency**: EUR only. **Min**: 0.50 EUR. **Max**: varies by customer's bank. **Customers**: Germany. **Business**: 30 European countries.
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown:
Wero (`wero`) is a standalone pan-European authenticated bank transfer method. Customers connect a bank account to their Wero wallet and approve in the app. The May 5, 2026 method overview listed German customers. November 7 lists Belgium, France, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands, separately from the unchanged 30 listed Stripe account countries. The cross-method overview labels Wero public preview. The separately documented [[stripe-ideal|iDEAL/Wero]] route uses `ideal` and has its own dated migration guidance.

**Amount and currency.** EUR only, with a EUR 0.50 minimum and a maximum that varies by the customer's bank. See [[source-stripe-wero]].
warnings: May method lines 8–18 and 52–85 and November method lines 9–19, 53–86 and 122–124 document the standalone scope. Compare the separate November payment-method overview lines 41–42 and 75–83 and iDEAL overview lines 11–30.

- **Refunds.** Full and partial refunds are documented, with multiple partial refunds up to the original amount. May states up to two years and November specifies 730 days from payment.
- **Connect.** Both method overviews list support. November also lists prohibited or restricted categories, including payment facilitators processing for sub-merchants.
